transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-21 14:30 UTC | Duration 46m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Elliot Vera (Redwood CSM); Marcus Lane, Aisha Rahman, Ben Ortiz, Priya Nair, Leo Wang (Helios Financial)

Summary:
Quick sync to confirm onboarding progress, unblock access paths, and validate early microbenchmarks. Big themes: staging gateway creds, VPC peering details, KMS/HSM questions, and a short e2e latency run. Aim to have a tight handoff to SREs by end of next week.

Topics covered:
- Access sequencing and temporary creds
- Network routing and peering (VPC, subnet, NAT)
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache behavior
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, RBAC
- Next-step benchmarks and acceptance tests

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — can folks see my screen?
[00:06] Marcus Lane: Yep, we can see it. morning, Jordan. Aisha, Ben on our side as well.
[00:10] Jordan Kim: Great. today it's a short sprint checkpoint, we're calling it the "Ops Orbit" sync — mostly unblock creds, net config, and run a short e2e bench. Priya, want to kick off with infra status?
[00:22] Priya Desai: Sure. Hi team. from Redwood side I confirmed that the staging gateway is ready to accept inbound peering, we just need the CIDR and the routes from Helios. the gateway will support token-based temporary creds or mTLS depending on your preference.
[00:35] Aisha Rahman: Quick Q — does the gateway require AWS PrivateLink or will standard peering be fine? we have govcloud constraints on some of the subnets.
[00:42] Priya Desai: Good question. For this pilot we support both. PrivateLink would avoid exposing routes, but standard VPC peering is simpler and lower friction. if you have strict compliance, PrivateLink + VPC endpoints is recommended.
[00:54] Leo Wang: We prefer peering for now, but need to validate NAT and egress rules — can you confirm egress IPs?
[00:59] Priya Desai: We'll provide the egress ranges and the ELB IP list — we'll put that in the shared doc.
[01:05] Jordan Kim: Also calling out the creds flow — Elliot will walk through the temporary token flow that most teams use to avoid handing long-lived keys.
[01:12] Elliot Vera: Hey all. The short version: we hand you a short-lived token via the console/email; you can exchange it at the gateway for a session token tied to your SSO. This avoids you needing to manage HSM keys initially. Long-term, if you want KMS/HSM integration, we support BYOK with HSM-backed keys.
[01:27] Priya Nair: On that, does Redwood rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation through our KMS?
[01:33] Priya Desai: For hosted onboarding, Redwood rotates service keys. For private deployments or with BYOK, rotation is your responsibility via your KMS; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM gateways.
[01:43] Marcus Lane: Good. security looks acceptable at a high level, but we need the SOC2 snapshot and audit log retention policy to present to legal.
[01:50] Jordan Kim: Absolutely, we'll send the security pack today.
[01:53] Priya Desai: I'll also include an example audit log extract and retention options — we support up to 7 years in enterprise plans, but default is 90 days for hosted.
[02:03] Ben Ortiz: about the bench — what payload are we running? we want something that mirrors our product: multi-turn chat with 3 retrieval calls and 400–700 tokens.
[02:12] Priya Desai: For a quick run we suggested a 512-token generation profile, simulating KV cache cold start for a subset of requests, and a continuous-batching profile for throughput. we'll run both latency and p50/p95 p99 tail numbers.
[02:25] Leo Wang: tail numbers are the big concern — if p99 is above our SLO of 300ms we'll need to discuss dedicated vs hosted.
[02:33] Priya Desai: yes. today we'll just capture the baseline on staging. if p99 spikes, we can try a quantized variant or fall back to a smaller model to meet SLOs. there's always the tradeoff: smaller model = lower latency and cost but some quality regression.
[02:48] Marcus Lane: Do you have previous baselines for similar customers? e.g., 8k context models on A100 or Ampere?
[02:55] Priya Desai: We do. I can share anonymized results — for 8k context on a 80/GTX-like cluster (note: this might be transcribed wrong, she meant Ampere), p50 was ~60ms per token in ideal conditions; p99 varied depending on batching and prefix cache hits.
[03:12] Jordan Kim: (laughing) the transcript engine likes to change Ampere to "a mower" sometimes.
[03:16] (laughter)
[03:18] Jordan Kim: Let's walk through the checklist so we have clear blockers. I'll read and you guys confirm. first: staging gateway creds — outstanding. second: VPC peering CIDR and route table snapshot — outstanding. third: KMS questions — customer to send list. fourth: quick e2e bench — Redwood to run and send logs. fifth: gating acceptance criteria doc — Marcus to finalize.
[03:34] Marcus Lane: confirmed. I'll add acceptance tests around p50/p95/p99 and token cost per 1k.
[03:40] Priya Nair: On the encryption side, one ask — does Redwood support customer-side encryption for logs in transit? we need to ensure audit logs do not retain plaintext payload.
[03:50] Priya Desai: We redact user-level content in standard retention exports and can apply envelope encryption with your KMS. We'll include configuration for log masking in the pack.
[03:58] Ben Ortiz: Quick product question: how do rollout policies work? we want canary for a model switch with traffic split and automatic rollback.
[04:06] Samir Patel: We offer canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks — you can split traffic per route and set thresholds on model latency and error rate to trigger rollback. There's also a staged config to pin specific model versions per tenant.
[04:18] Ben Ortiz: ok, that helps for our risk policy.
[04:21] Jordan Kim: Time for the short bench run — Priya, are you ready to kick it off?
[04:26] Priya Desai: yes. we'll run the 512 token profile, 1000 requests at ramped concurrency to mirror your peak. we'll post p50/p95/p99 and a CSV of latencies.
[04:36] (typing sounds)
[04:38] Priya Desai: running now — starting warmups to populate KV cache for 100 requests, then cold-run for 200 to measure initial miss.
[04:48] Leo Wang: while that's running, a quick network detail: are source IPs stable for the session so we can whitelist?
[04:54] Priya Desai: We'll provide an egress range but sessions can flow through different IPs behind the ELB; for strict whitelisting we recommend mTLS or PrivateLink.
[05:03] Marcus Lane: noted.
[05:06] (brief pause while bench runs)
[06:12] Priya Desai: Ok initial numbers — p50 78ms, p95 220ms, p99 540ms for the cold-run (512 tokens). warm-run p50 45ms, p95 120ms, p99 260ms. attaching logs to the chat after the call.
[06:27] Marcus Lane: p99 540ms cold is a red flag for us for some flows. what's the knob we should try first? batching, smaller model, dedicated?
[06:36] Priya Desai: First quick lever is to enable prefix KV caching aggressively for your retrieval patterns — that reduces cold miss cost. second is to reduce sequence length where possible, third is to bump to dedicated capacity to cut scheduling jitter; last would be model size.
[06:48] Jordan Kim: Also we can tune continuous batching thresholds to favor latency over throughput for specific routes.
[06:54] Ben Ortiz: what's the cost delta on dedicated? ballpark numbers are fine for now.
[06:59] Jordan Kim: Ballpark, dedicated cuts per-token cost by ~20–40% at scale and reduces p99 tail by eliminating multi-tenant scheduling, but you pay for reserved GPUs monthly. we'll send a concise pricing comparison.
[07:12] Priya Desai: One more datapoint — quantized variants can reduce latency and cost but watch for slight quality drift. we can run an A/B on a subset of traffic.
[07:21] Marcus Lane: ok. For next steps here we need the security docs and VPC details to proceed to full staging, and we need the bench CSV to decide if we test canary or go dedicated.
[07:31] Jordan Kim: Agreed. Elliot will update the onboarding runbook with the temporary creds flow and links. We'll close the loop with the security pack today.
[07:38] Elliot Vera: I'll also add a short playbook for fallbacks: if p99 > 400ms, route 10% of traffic to fallback model and increase cache TTL.
[07:46] Priya Nair: That playbook looks good — please include audit steps for verifying masked logs.
[07:51] Priya Desai: Will do.
[07:53] Jordan Kim: any other blockers from Helios?
[07:56] Aisha Rahman: none besides the network and creds items we've discussed — we'll get the CIDR and route snapshot by tomorrow.
[08:03] Marcus Lane: and we'll aim to finalize acceptance criteria by Friday the 28th.
[08:08] Jordan Kim: Perfect. quick recap — action items in the chat, we'll follow up with the bench logs, security pack, and pricing. Expect the staging creds email by 2026-12-23.
[08:18] Ben Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[08:20] Jordan Kim: Thanks all — speak soon.

End of transcript.
